chapter_theme: Rules for the disciple and a polemic against the gurus of the world: the mind made an atom and sent to the crown, the kalpa herbs and the nectar reread as inner things, ochre-robed teachers who sell instruction, and siddhas who built rival sastras. The disciple then asks where lives go when all the eggs are void, and the teacher answers with his own history through the dissolutions: Vishnu asleep on the banyan leaf gathering lives in his lotus, the pillar of fire with the androgynous queen within it, creation handed back to Vishnu, and Kakapusundar surviving each pralaya as a crow on the northern mountain.
structure_note: Method and conduct for the disciple (2351 to 2357); the false gurus and the bookish siddhas (2358 to 2360); the true jnani and the forehead eye (2361 to 2363); the disciple's question on the void (2364) and the teacher's narrative of pralaya, the fire-pillar and creation (2365 to 2373); the teacher's longevity and the return of the mind to the crown (2374 to 2375).

2351.reading: Know that the mind itself becomes life, and joining the egg is release; one can ride the horse; the five great sins fly away; making the wide mind an atom and seeing the fate of what is left and what is touched, the sign called kundali is the crown of the egg, and he tells it as the state of the triangle.
2351.nuance: பரி, the horse, is the Siddhars' usual cipher for the breath, so riding it is breath-mastery; a plain reading of a horse is not meaningful here. முக்கோணம், the triangle, is in tantra the seat at the root; Kakapusundar moves it, with kundalini, to the crown. விட்டகுறை தொட்டகுறை is the karmic remainder from past lives.

2352.reading: Do not go about among the men of the world but stand alone; do not overeat; do not speak a one-sided judgement; do not forget the letter; do not wander wearily; do not consort with one possessed by the demon of lust; see the Cause and play.
2352.nuance: A rule-list in negatives. ஓமென்ற and ஆமென்ற அட்சரம் carry the syllable Om and its affirming form; the letter not to be forgotten is the unspoken letter of 2338 rather than a recited mantra, on the chapter's own terms.

2353.reading: Play, pluck and eat the karunelli: the head will not cook, so look with desire; catch and eat the white rat-snake, son, and it becomes the undying leg; drink the milk of the flame without wavering; the pillar of fire has become the sushumna; join the four kalai that are going to the eight, and see the guileless body.
2353.nuance: A plain reading has a herb (கருநெல்லி, black gooseberry) and a snake (வெண்சாரை) eaten as kalpa; in the Siddhars' cipher both are names for the inner nectar and the breath, and the third line, drinking the milk of the flame, is inner on any reading. The verse is history of a claim, not a recipe. கலைநாலு ... எட்டில் is unexplained; the four and the eight may be breath-measures or the moon's digits.

2354.reading: Seeing and seeing, as the mind goes to the egg the four kalai and the eight merge; do not act at odds, for if the mind turns elsewhere you will never know the Supreme; serve and approach the great ones, son, worship and hear this book with love; if they will not tell you, this book will; keep the mind restrained and win.
2354.nuance: The book offers itself as a substitute guru, இந்நூல் சொல்லும், while still telling the disciple to serve the great ones; 2360 explains the distrust.

2355.reading: Vain men speak of a vidya-mantra; leap instead to the hill of vidya, son, for when you climb and look it shows the transcendent vidya-mantra without end; seeing that state you will do creation and destruction in a minute; nectar bubbles up and you may eat the fruit that has no other.
2355.nuance: விஞ்சை is vidya as magic; the verse turns the magician's mantra into the hill of the crown. The claim to create and destroy in a minute is the siddha's share in the Lord's five acts.

2356.reading: One can eat it: when absorbed in Brahman it melts and flows in the firm egg; the sugar of nectar appears, sweet with milk, firmly, son; one can stay there, the body unknowing, and the coat slips off and it is like gold; by the lamp of true knowledge, swelling, look: the world is one.
2356.nuance: சட்டை கழன்று, the coat slipping off, is the snake-skin image: either the body is shed, or the old skin is shed and the body turns gold, the kaya siddhi of 2380. திங்கலாம் may be a verb form or the moon; the nectar from the moon is the usual yogic account.

2357.reading: The one Brahman, as many, became an endless dance in the world: good and evil and the four, the names sun and moon, mountains and endless creeping things, and the marks called guru and disciple; fix with one mind on the Lord in whom nada and bindu have subsided.
2357.nuance: The list includes குருக்கள் and சீடன் among the appearances of the One, which answers the trouble of 2349: the guru-disciple pair is real as a mark, not as a second thing.

2358.reading: The siddhas all set up differences and built sastras as if for good; men locked onto the books and never saw the egg in full; like a deer wandering the forest they speak deceitful mouth-jnana; they do not see the cuckoo shut in the cage; see the sign of the unspoken mantra.
2358.nuance: வாய்ஞானம், jnana of the mouth, is the Siddhars' phrase for learned talk. The cuckoo in the cage is the life or the inner sound in the body, by the usual cipher. The complaint against the siddhas' own books returns as a charge of concealment in 2393.

2359.reading: The gurus of this world of signs scrutinise the harsh Vedas yet, not knowing Brahman, proudly slander the great; putting on an ample disguise and wearing ochre, they roam for show like dogs, mockingly carrying the staff and walking hunched over the earth.
2359.nuance: காவி (ochre) and தண்டு (the staff) are the marks of the sannyasi; the verse attacks the garb, not renunciation. குறட்டிட்டு நடப்பான் pictures the affected stoop of a holy man.

2360.reading: The sinner calls disciples and says he will give instruction to take their money; showing no state of Brahman he tells lies as wide as the sky; it becomes sin for the disciple and a flaw for the guru who prescribes fixity; he does not see the place where things subside, and when it fails he says it was ended by fate.
2360.nuance: The guru's appeal to விதி, fate, is the mark of the fraud: he explains his pupil's failure by destiny because he never knew the place. 2329 had already removed fate from Brahman.

2361.reading: Entering the egg called the sky, seeing the lamp at the centre of the crown of the northern mountain, bathing in the pure Siva-Ganga called honey and putting on the holy name, offering the loving mind as the flower, seeing the harsh Vedas subside, chitta becoming buddhi: those who are clear in this are true jnanis.
2361.nuance: Every rite rejected in 2347 and 2348 returns inside: the tirtha is the Ganga at the crown, the name-mark and the flower are the mind's love. வடவரை, the northern mountain, is Meru and the head.

2362.reading: When you see the egg as one, the many differing mayas flee in panic; you will stand as yourself in every life born in the egg, the whole-egg and the Brahma-egg; when the forehead eye opens it shows mingled all the sights the eye cannot hold; the upper circle, the wide wheel: follow and join it in the space of true knowledge.
2362.nuance: உயிர்தோறும் நீயாய் நிற்பாய், you stand as yourself in every life, is the verse's claim of pervasion, made for the seer rather than for the Lord.

2363.reading: Joining is this: with the mind one and knowing its nature, not dancing about but attentive, not reading many books, going to the space at the centre of Parapara's crown, watching the dance of 'thondhom', seeing the thousand and eight petals tier on tier, know the lamp that does not fade, like rain on withering crops.
2363.nuance: தொந்தோம் is a dance syllable, and may also carry தொம் and தத், the thou and that of the great saying; the verse does not settle it. ஆயிரத்தெட்டிதழ், a thousand and eight petals, is the crown lotus, usually a thousand. பலநூலைப் படித்திடாமல் makes the refusal of books a condition.

2364.reading: The disciple asks: you have spoken true knowledge and the foot of the state of Parapara; but when all the eggs become void and the Virat Brahman alone stands as one, where are all the lives, where are the siddhas and the three murtis, where is the place that water rests? Guru, tell me this.
2364.nuance: The question is cosmological, where souls are during dissolution, and the answer that follows (2365 to 2373) is a Puranic narrative rather than a yogic one, the only such stretch in the work.

2365.reading: He will tell, son Vasinatha: in the assembly of the gracious Isvara, at the time of the pralaya that tests, Vimala asked Vishnu where living beings, siddhas and sages were to stay, and the cloud-bodied one looked at him, bowed, and considered his answer.
2365.nuance: The scene is told as witnessed; Kakapusundar places himself in Siva's court at the dissolution, as 2366 confirms.

2366.reading: Vishnu will think: I sleep on the banyan leaf, and the weighty living beings and endless siddhas will gather firmly in my lotus, and I will stand sustaining them; and when Vishnu with his bearer said that Pusundar too would come, Siva called me as the sruti and asked, and I spoke good words as a sutra.
2366.nuance: The infant Vishnu on the banyan leaf in the waters of dissolution is the Puranic Markandeya scene. வலவன் may be the charioteer or Garuda. The teacher is summoned as சுருதி, as if he were scripture, a large claim made in passing.

2367.reading: Looking at Siva's face: when all the lives of countless crores of eggs, with the siddhas and sages, and Vishnu too sleep on the banyan leaf, they gather by nature in the lotus of the navel; and passing beyond the five I came swiftly by the street-way.
2367.nuance: ஐவர், the five, are probably the five gods of the five acts (Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, Mahesvara, Sadasiva); வீதிவழி, the street-way, may be the sushumna. The poet claims to pass beyond the gods who are themselves dissolved.

2368.reading: Going through the sky, child, the wheel spun and danced; mounting the wheel without slipping I went beyond it; going a long way I surely saw the state of the pillar; it stands spread like fire, and no space or anything else could be seen.
2368.nuance: சக்கரம் here is the spinning wheel of the cosmos or of the crown, which the seer rides past; கம்பம், the pillar of fire, is Siva as the lingodbhava column, the form in which neither Brahma nor Vishnu could find his ends.

2369.reading: The pillar of fire is everywhere as one; in the pillar's middle a queen stands united; oho, when I looked at her face, seen from the front it was a male form and seen from behind a female form, son; and I stayed within the pillar as substance with substance.
2369.nuance: The androgyne in the pillar is Ardhanarisvara, Siva and Shakti as one body; the poet's claim to have remained there வத்தோடே வத்தாக, substance with substance, is a claim of identity with it.

2370.reading: So for endless time I lived within Parapara; when Brahman relented and gave grace to create the whole, the woman who was in the pillar appeared both as Vimala and as Uma, and from within the wheel she called Vishnu: see the resolve.
2370.nuance: Creation begins as grace (அருள்) and a relenting (மனமிரங்கி) in Brahman; the agent is Shakti, who takes both Siva's and Uma's forms, and Vishnu is her instrument.

2371.reading: Vishnu in the lotus called out all the lives of countless crores of eggs, showed them the three gunas, and set out the standing oceans and the earth, the sun and moon, the rising mountains, forests and living beings, the nine planets and the stars, and the four Vedas.
2371.nuance: The Vedas are listed last among created things, after the planets, which is the cosmological form of the chapter's argument that scripture is not the way.

2372.reading: Making gods and elements, sky and earth in the world, Meru and the mountains, temples, tirthas and tanks, with Brahman alone as witness he filled every life everywhere; without roaming, see silence, and listen to more so as to win.
2372.nuance: கோவில், தீர்த்தம் and குளம் are placed among created things beside mountains and elements, which relativises them without denying them.

2373.reading: So when the pralayas have numbered seven lakh crores, Hari and Ayan and living things are absorbed in the Brahman called the whole; I too go that way; and when it again becomes the whole, I took the form of the crow and perched in the nest of the northern mountain.
2373.nuance: The grammar of lines six and seven is loose: whether the crow form is taken at each re-creation or once is not clear. The crow (காகம்) is finally explained as the teacher's own body between creations, Meru's nest being the head.

2374.reading: So through the yugas I have been on earth, how many crores of times; is there anyone who knows as I do? I became the beginning of the primal siddhi; when I went to Vimala's place he lifted me with joy and kissed me and told me to stay on Kailasa; I remained in the crow form.
2374.nuance: ஆதியென்ற சித்திக்கும் ஆதியானேன் claims that Kakapusundar is the origin of siddhi itself; the kiss from Siva makes him a child of the god rather than a pupil.

2375.reading: In the crow form, watching all the causes as seed, watching steadily the race of the open space, I circled far and still saw no detail; then, making the spread mind an atom with longing, forcing the supreme space to become the mind's space, reaching the egg, I came to the middle of the centre of the crown.
2375.nuance: The cosmic narrative ends by returning to method: the outer search over vast distance fails, and the mind made an atom at the crown succeeds. The last line's முச்சி is உச்சி in sandhi.

links.note: Both say the One itself stands as its opposites and its gods: Tirumular's Lord is the three lights in one, stands as Brahma and Vishnu, as space, light and darkness; Kakapusundar's one Brahman becomes good and evil, sun and moon, guru and disciple.

2349 condemns those who multiply gods and call this one guru and that one disciple instead of approaching Brahman; 2357 allows guru and disciple as marks the one Brahman takes. The pair is real as appearance, false as a second thing.

Tirumular's jnani is one who comes to see all the good books of the earth together with the way of silence and the end of the unwritten Veda; Kakapusundar says those locked onto the siddhas' books never see the egg. Tirumular includes books in what the jnani sees; Kakapusundar excludes them, so this narrows rather than contradicts.
Both say the ascetic's outward form without the inner strength is a disguise: the Kural's cow grazing in a tiger's skin, Kakapusundar's robed and staffed guru roaming like a dog.

The Kural says neither shaving nor matted hair is needed if one gives up what the world condemns; Kakapusundar mocks the ochre, the staff and the stoop as show. Both make the marks of renunciation worthless without the thing itself.

Both define the false guru by what he does with the teaching: Tirumular's has looked over mantra, yoga and jnana yet goes blind for the sake of food; Kakapusundar's gathers disciples to take their money and blames fate when his instruction fails.

Tirumular says those who know only bathing cannot join the Lord, who is in the minds of those whose knowledge is clear; Kakapusundar's tirtha is the Siva-Ganga at the crown and his flower the loving mind, and the clear (தெளிந்தவர்) are the true jnanis.
2348 rejects bathing a linga and offering plucked flowers; 2361 keeps bathing, name-mark and flower-offering as inner acts at the crown. The rite is not abolished but moved inside.
2345 opens the forehead eye and finds the earth filled as one; 2362 says what it shows: the sights the ordinary eye cannot hold, and the seer standing as himself in every life.

Both say that at dissolution the works of Vishnu and Brahma sink back into the source: Tirumular's crop of the waste returns to the waste, Kakapusundar's Hari and Ayan and all lives are absorbed in the whole Brahman. Both also keep a remainder that does not perish: the waste itself, and the crow on Meru.

new_concepts.gloss: Brahman: the Supreme (also பரப்பிரமம், பராபரம்) from which gods, lives and eggs issue and into which mind, breath and worlds are absorbed; Kakapusundar's name for the goal of the whole practice
new_concepts.label_source: Used in nearly every verse, as பிரமம் (2329, 2340), பரப்பிரமம் (2334, 2336) and பராபரம் (2326, 2364)

new_concepts.gloss: the crown of the egg: the top of the head taken as the summit of the cosmos, the one place where body and universe are the same egg and where the mind is to be fixed
new_concepts.label_source: Used as அண்ட வுச்சி in 2327, 2329, 2331, 2336, 2337, 2338, 2342, 2344 and throughout the work

new_concepts.gloss: sushumna, the central channel, which Kakapusundar places in the skull at the brow-centre and the uvula rather than along the spine
new_concepts.label_source: The verses write சுழுனை (2327, 2334, 2336, 2339, 2353); சுழுமுனை is the standard form

new_concepts.gloss: kalpa: the rejuvenating preparation of the medical siddhas, which keeps the body from ageing, and the inner practice that is said to replace it

source_issues: 2366: வருதியாய் is an odd form, perhaps for வருவதாய்.
2373: the syntax of நலமாக இன்னமுந்தான் அகண்ட மானால் is loose; whether the crow form is taken at each re-creation or once is unclear.
2375: நடுவணைய முச்சிநடு has உச்சி written as முச்சி by sandhi.
